experiment.title: 'Done' is not proof. Here's what a receipt actually contains.
experiment.hook: 'done' is a claim. a receipt is proof.
experiment.hypothesis: A word-kill callout hook ('done is not proof') plus a 5-field receipt-anatomy list tests whether reframing a familiar word out-reaches a problem-first hook for cold traffic + saves.
experiment.caption:
the thing that finally broke me on agent workflows was realizing i didn't trust a single 'done' i got back. an agent would come back all confident, task complete, and i'd still open every file and re-read every diff, because 'done' just means the agent stopped — it says nothing about whether the work is right. and so i'm re-auditing everything by hand, which means the autonomy never compounds, i'm just a slower reviewer with extra steps. so the fix isn't a better status message. the artifact has to come back as the receipt: version, provenance, how it was evaluated, what review state it's in, what it cost, all bolted to the thing itself. and then proof rooms + embedded mcp widgets render that state right inside claude or cursor so you're never leaving to go verify. the whole idea is you read the receipt instead of redoing the work...

#aiagents #mcp #buildinpublic #aiops #claude #agentic #devtools #trustbutverify

slides.headline: 'done' is a claim. a receipt is proof.
slides.subtext: you still open the file to check. every single time.

slides.headline: 'done' tells you the agent stopped. not that the work is right.
slides.subtext: stopped and correct are two completely different states.

slides.headline: so you audit everything by hand. and the autonomy stops compounding.
slides.subtext: every manual re-check is where the leverage leaks out.

slides.headline: the artifact is the receipt.
slides.subtext: work should come back as evidence, not an announcement.

slides.kicker: what a receipt carries — save this
slides.headline: a proof return ships with 5 things attached:
slides.subtext: version · provenance · evaluation · review state · cost

slides.headline: proof rooms + MCP widgets put the state inside the client you already use.
slides.subtext: no new dashboard to babysit. it renders in claude, cursor, wherever you are.

slides.headline: you stop re-checking. you read the receipt and move.
slides.subtext: autonomy is useful. continuity is what makes it compound.

slides.headline: if your agent said 'done' right now, could you prove it?
slides.subtext: this is the layer i'm building at useorgx.com. follow for the next teardown.
